title: France’s government debt is a commercial real estate problem
gist: France's political deadlock is driving government debt higher and pushing up bond yields, which Oxford Economics expects to weigh on an already weak French commercial real estate market over the next five years, though tourism-linked hotel, retail and industrial segments offer selective bright spots.

insights.claim: France's political deadlock is causing government debt to keep rising, and markets are pricing more risk into French government bonds, which is expected to push bond yields higher and weigh on France's commercial real estate recovery.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Watch French sovereign bond yields as a leading indicator for further downside in French CRE valuations and financing costs.
insights.quote: Political deadlock means France’s government debt will continue rising, and that has markets pricing more risk for owning government bonds. We expect higher bond yields will weigh on France’s commercial real estate recovery.
insights.locator: Political deadlock means France's government debt

insights.claim: French commercial real estate values are forecast to keep declining this year, and France is expected to be one of Europe's weakest-performing commercial real estate markets over the next five years.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: A multi-year underperformance call flags France as a market to underweight relative to European CRE peers.
insights.quote: France is expected to be one of Europe’s weakest-performing commercial real estate markets over the next five years.
insights.locator: The outlook for French commercial real estate is challenging

insights.claim: The weak French commercial real estate outlook is driven specifically by the country's strained growth outlook combined with high exposure to the office sector.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Office-heavy French portfolios carry outsized downside risk versus other property types in the same market.
insights.quote: given the country’s strained growth outlook and high exposure to the office sector
insights.locator: The outlook for French commercial real estate is challenging

themes.theme: Tourism and retail as offsetting bright spots

insights.claim: Despite the bleak macro and office-sector outlook, tourism growth and e-commerce expansion are expected to support performance in France's hotel, retail, and industrial real estate segments.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Investors avoiding French CRE broadly should still consider selective exposure to hotel, retail, and industrial assets rather than a blanket exit.
insights.quote: Tourism growth and e-commerce expansion will support hotel, retail, and industrial performance.

insights.claim: France is one of the world's top tourism destinations, and Paris ranks first in Europe for international visitor spending, underpinning demand for hotel and retail commercial real estate.
insights.speaker: Duncan Campbell
insights.so_what: Paris's top-ranked international visitor spending supports a case for selective hotel/retail asset picking even as broader French CRE weakens.
insights.quote: France is notably one of the world’s top tourism destinations and Paris ranks first in Europe for international visitor spending.
